title: $\overline{\mathbf Q}_{\ell }$-coefficient pairing
statement:
In the Poincare duality conventions of this chapter (the fixed setting), let $K\in D^b_c(X,\overline{\mathbf Q}_{\ell })$ be perfect over the coefficient sheaf and be represented by an object over some finite $E/\mathbf Q_{\ell }$. The derived Poincare pairing of [def-pod-derived-poincare-pairing] preserves the corresponding direct summands and is independent of every further finite extension; it defines the perfect derived and degreewise pairings over $\overline{\mathbf Q}_{\ell }$, whose adjoint has inverse the canonical isomorphism

$$
R\Gamma _c(X,K)^\vee \xrightarrow {\  \sim \  } R\Gamma \bigl(X,K^\vee (d)\bigr)[2d]
$$

in the $\overline{\mathbf Q}_{\ell }$-category of [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients]. The degreewise pairings $H_c^i(X,K)\times H^{2d-i}(X,K^\vee(d))\to\overline{\mathbf Q}_{\ell }$ over the field $\overline{\mathbf Q}_{\ell }$ are perfect, the trace $\operatorname {tr}_X:H_c^{2d}(X,\overline{\mathbf Q}_{\ell }(d))\to\overline{\mathbf Q}_{\ell }$ and its untwisted form $\operatorname {tr}^{(-d)}_X:H_c^{2d}(X,\overline{\mathbf Q}_{\ell })\to\overline{\mathbf Q}_{\ell }(-d)$ are isomorphisms (on $H^{2d}$ in place of $H_c^{2d}$ if $X_0$ is proper), and the Frobenius similitude of [cor-pod-untwisted-similitude] holds.

proof.text: Choose a finite coefficient field $E$ and a site-perfect representative $K_E$. This is the meaning of perfectness at the common stage in [def-pod-perfect-complex-on-x]; enlarge the field of a previously chosen representative if necessary. Put $C_E=R\Gamma_c(X,K_E)$ and $D_E=R\Gamma(X,K_E^\vee(d))[2d]$. Apply [thm-pod-derived-poincare-duality] at $\Lambda=E$: the pairing $\beta_E:C_E\otimes_E^L D_E\to E$ has adjoint $a_E:D_E\to C_E^\vee$ with canonical inverse $u_E:C_E^\vee\to D_E$. All its hypotheses hold in the fixed smooth separated finite-type setting; properness is unnecessary. By [thm-pod-degreewise-perfectness-over-a-field] at $E$, its degreewise pairings have finite-dimensional factors and invertible adjoints. The scalar-extension compatibility in the derived theorem identifies these maps, including $u_E$, with the corresponding maps after every finite extension $L/E$.

source.place: Proof, first sentence: finite E representative and E-level perfectness

proof.text: Use the common-stage category [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients]. For any two representatives choose a common finite extension, form their tensor products, duals and the pairing there, and take the resulting morphism class. The comparisons of step 1 identify $\beta_L$ with the extension of $\beta_E$. Thus enlarging the field gives the same class. If the representative of $K$ changes by an isomorphism represented at a common stage, naturality of the derived pairing identifies the two classes at that stage. The descent rule [prop-weil-pbc-descent-functors], including its clause on compatible natural transformations and equations, identifies the descended operations and maps with these classes. The descended pairing is specifically the composite of cup product, evaluation and normalized smooth trace in [def-pod-derived-poincare-pairing], rather than a separately chosen perfect form. The orientation used in that trace is the transported canonical purity orientation: apply [thm-pur-rational-and-qbar-purity] to $a_X$ and the coefficient unit. Its lattice is the constant integral unit, so the lattice hypothesis of that theorem is satisfied. This fixes the canonical identification in the asserted formula.

source.place: Proof, descent of pairings, independence of extensions and transport of purity

proof.text: Represent $a$ and $u$ by $a_E$ and $u_E$ from step 1. Both equations $a_Eu_E=1$ and $u_Ea_E=1$ hold at that finite stage, hence hold in the common-stage Hom groups by their definition in [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients]. Thus $u$ is precisely the inverse of the descended adjoint $a$, and gives the displayed canonical isomorphism $R\Gamma_c(X,K)^\vee\simeq R\Gamma(X,K^\vee(d))[2d]$. This is perfectness in [def-pod-perfect-derived-pairing]. No inference from degreewise perfectness to derived perfectness is being made here.

source.place: Proof, the pairing and its adjoint are well defined and perfect

proof.text: For the direct-summand assertion, let $e:K\to K$ be an idempotent. By [prop-weil-pbc-common-stage-calculus], its equation $e^2=e$ and any chosen splitting maps can be represented over one sufficiently large finite field. Splittings exist by [thm-weil-pbc-idempotent-complete-triangulation]; this is a property of the common-stage category, not a further Karoubi completion. On the two cohomology factors let $p=R\Gamma_c(e)$ and $r=R\Gamma(e^\vee(d))[2d]$. Naturality of the evaluation in [def-pod-coefficient-dual-on-x] and of the pairing in [thm-pod-derived-poincare-duality] gives $\beta(p\otimes1)=\beta(1\otimes r)$ and hence $ar=p^\vee a$. Since $u=a^{-1}$, also $ru=up^\vee$. If $i_C:C'\to C$, $s_C:C\to C'$ and $i_D:D'\to D$, $s_D:D\to D'$ split $p$ and $r$, the restricted adjoint and inverse are $i_C^\vee a i_D$ and $s_Du s_C^\vee$. Their composites are identities: insert $i_Ds_D=r$, $i_Cs_C=p$, the two displayed intertwining identities, and $s_Ci_C=s_Di_D=1$. Thus the pairing pairs each summand with its dual summand and is perfect on it. These equations are finite-stage equations, so the same common-stage rule makes the restriction independent of further extension.

source.place: Statement direct-summand clause; proof idempotent-complete common-stage paragraph

proof.text: By [def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology], these cohomology groups are those of the coefficient complexes at the point. In [def-weil-point-fd-qlbar-category], transition is termwise exact scalar extension and satisfies $H^j(T_{L/E}A)=H^j(A)\otimes_E L$. Consequently the vector-space reading over $\Qlb$ of a stage-$E$ cohomology space $V$ is $V\otimes_E\Qlb$: every vector has finitely many coefficients in $\Qlb$, lying in a common finite extension. Apply this to the finite-dimensional spaces of step 1. In finite bases, the matrix of each degreewise adjoint and its inverse over $E$ still multiply to the identity over every $L$ and over $\Qlb$. Their scalar extensions are exactly the degreewise adjoints of the descended pairing, by the scalar-extension and degree-indexing compatibility in [thm-pod-derived-poincare-duality]. This proves the asserted degreewise perfectness, including zero cohomology degrees.

Apply [thm-pod-trace-isomorphism] at the field stage $E$ to the constant sheaf with its canonical Weil datum. It gives both $H_c^{2d}(X,E(d))\simeq E$ and $H_c^{2d}(X,E)\simeq E(-d)$, and identifies these maps with the normalized smooth trace used above. The same descended trace maps and their inverses therefore give the claimed $\Qlb$ isomorphisms. When $X_0$ is proper, use also the proper clause of that theorem, $H_c^{2d}=H^{2d}$; no such replacement is made otherwise. For the Frobenius assertion take the strict Weil structure required by [cor-pod-untwisted-similitude], as stipulated by [def-pod-conventions]. Represent its isomorphism and the pairing at a common finite coefficient stage. That corollary gives $\langle F_c x,F_{K^\vee}y\rangle^{\mathrm{untw}}=q^d\langle x,y\rangle^{\mathrm{untw}}$ there. The Frobenius maps in the conventions are stagewise; applying the descent rule for transformations and equations in [prop-weil-pbc-descent-functors] gives the same equality in the common-stage category and on the scalar-extended cohomology spaces. Bilinearity then gives it on all vectors over $\Qlb$. For the constant object its datum is canonical, yielding the stated constant-coefficient similitude.

proof.text: Represent $K$ by an $E$-object $K_E\in D^b_{ctf}(X,E)$ over the finite $E/\mathbf Q_{\ell }$ stage of the common-stage construction. The $E$-level pairing is perfect by [thm-pod-degreewise-perfectness-over-a-field], and the equivariance by [cor-pod-untwisted-similitude]; the trace isomorphism (in its compact-support form, and on $H^{2d}$ when $X_0$ is proper) is the $E$-level case of [thm-pod-trace-isomorphism]. Finite extension of the coefficient field transports all of it by [thm-pod-adic-reconstruction-and-scalar-extension]; the descent of the pairings to the common-stage category and the independence of the further extensions are the descent functors of [prop-weil-pbc-descent-functors], with the common-stage category of [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients] idempotent complete by the filtered-retract-descent theorem of [thm-weil-pbc-idempotent-complete-triangulation] (so its presentation by an idempotent is unnecessary), and the transport of the duality identification is the corresponding transport of the smooth purity, [thm-pur-rational-and-qbar-purity]. The pairing and its adjoint are thus well defined and perfect; the remaining assertions are the transported degreewise and similitude statements of the $E$-level case.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q15-4a66e9d22 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: PASS: the six steps hold as stated; the delivery has no new nodes and needs no fixes. The statement is the main-20261015 blueprint_update statement byte for byte, so nothing is weakened; the only change from master is removing the stray heading '9.7 The master interface'. proof_deps equals the union of the step uses, all three kinds of Mathlib search are recorded, no SGA source is cited, and no dependency of the item reaches back to it. Step 1: def-pod-perfect-complex-on-x, second paragraph, allows a site-perfect representative over a finite extension. thm-pod-derived-poincare-duality at Lambda=E gives the canonical inverse and scalar-extension compatibility without properness, and thm-pod-degreewise-perfectness-over-a-field at E gives the degreewise statement. Step 2 rests on the Hom-colimit definition of def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients and the equations clause of prop-weil-pbc-descent-functors. It applies thm-pur-rational-and-qbar-purity only to a_X and the unit, which has the lattice O_E, and Spec k meets that theorem's hypotheses. Step 3: a_E u_E=1 and u_E a_E=1 hold in the colimit Hom groups. Step 4: I redid the retract calculation from p=i_C s_C, r=i_D s_D, ar=p^vee a and ru=up^vee; both composites are the identity, and e=0, e=1 and a diagonal idempotent come out right. Step 5 uses H^i(T_{L/E}A)=H^i(A)⊗L from def-weil-point-fd-qlbar-category; zero degrees and d=0 work. Step 6 uses the E-stage trace theorem, with its proper clause only under properness, and the similitude corollary only under the required strict Weil structure. Dropping thm-pod-adic-reconstruction-and-scalar-extension is justified: it needs a site-perfect O_E-lattice that an arbitrary K_E may lack, and the E-stage input comes instead from sk-thm-derived-duality, a unit the transport unit cites. Accepted tool_uses: prop-weil-pbc-descent-functors, prop-weil-pbc-common-stage-calculus, thm-weil-pbc-idempotent-complete-triangulation and thm-pur-rational-and-qbar-purity. The other four declared tool uses are already on the unit's route and need no declaration. Caution for later: thm-pod-derived-poincare-duality and thm-pod-degreewise-perfectness-over-a-field already state the Qlbar case, and their future splits must not cite this item, or a cycle forms. The full step-by-step checks are in review.md.
